recentItems.title: Childhood friend steps up to save former News 12 reporter’s life with liver donation
recentItems.description:
After battling autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis for most of her life, former News 12 reporter Amy McGorry desperately needed a new liver. When childhood friend Susan Filshie saw Amy's story, she stepped forward, underwent testing, and was found to be a perfect donor match. Three months after their transplant surgery, both women are recovering and hope their journey inspires others to learn about living organ donation.

recentItems.title: Newark Airport launches facial recognition checkpoint for TSA PreCheck
recentItems.description:
A new facial recognition screening system is now operating at Newark Liberty International Airport's Terminal C. TSA PreCheck travelers who opt in through the United app can pass through security by scanning their face, with no physical ID required at the checkpoint. Officials say the technology is designed to streamline screening and help handle heavy holiday travel volumes.

recentItems.title: Dolly Parton corn maze becomes emotional tribute after her death
recentItems.description:
A 5-acre Dolly Parton-themed corn maze at Twins BBQ in Brookfield, Connecticut is welcoming visitors with trivia, music, story time and a special tribute to the country music legend. Planned before Parton's death, the maze now serves as a memorial while also celebrating the 31st anniversary of her Imagination Library. A portion of proceeds will support the children's literacy program that provides free books to young children.

Police believe the attack was targeted and say the investigation remains active.

recentItems.title: What’s moving into this Brooklyn department store? Developers reveal major new tenants
recentItems.description:
After sitting vacant since the Century 21 closure in 2020, the longtime Bay Ridge retail site is being transformed into a mixed-use development called Century Marketplace. Developers say Burlington has signed on and a mystery national grocery chain will become the first national grocer to serve southwest Brooklyn. While some welcome new retail options, local business owners are watching closely as the neighborhood continues to evolve.

For participants, the celebration is about more than costumes, it's a showcase of culture, unity and Caribbean pride.

recentItems.title: What went wrong? MTA worker killed by train while on the job
recentItems.description:
A multi-agency investigation is underway after the MTA says a worker was struck and killed by a train at the 161st Street-Yankee Stadium subway station. Sources close to the investigation say 41-year-old Moet McCullum was working on the tracks as a construction flagger when she was hit by a D train. The Transit Workers Union says McCullum was a mother of three and that workers and her family are devastated by the loss.

recentItems.title: Parolee charged in deadly Bronx bodega shooting indicted on 14 counts
recentItems.description:
A Bronx man accused of a deadly shooting inside a Mott Haven bodega has been indicted on 14 counts, including first-degree murder, manslaughter, robbery, and weapons charges. Prosecutors say Jesus Acosta fatally shot 33-year-old Tayvon Shuler, injured a bodega worker, and fired at three other people before fleeing. Authorities arrested Acosta after a weeklong manhunt, and he has pleaded not guilty. The Bronx shooting came two days after police say Acosta killed a 44-year-old man in a shooting at a Brownsville restaurant.
